title: Honor the one through whom life arrives
subtitle: Raag Aasaa
summary: The shabad begins by tracing birth, friendship, marriage, and lineage through woman. It then asks how she can be called bad when kings themselves are born from her, and ends in radiant mouths that praise the Lord.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels shaped by casual contempt, inherited patriarchy, or speech that lowers women while depending on them. Taken seriously, it restores reverence, humility, and a truer social imagination.
takeaway: Keep this in front of you: refuse to despise the one through whom human life comes.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡਿ ਜੰਮੀਐ ਭੰਡਿ ਨਿੰਮੀਐ ਭੰਡਿ ਮੰਗਣੁ ਵੀਆਹੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)dd ja(n)meeaai bha(n)dd ni(n)meeaai bha(n)dd ma(n)gan veeaahu ||
lines.translation: From woman, man is born; within woman, man is conceived; to woman he is engaged and married.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡਹੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਦੋਸਤੀ ਭੰਡਹੁ ਚਲੈ ਰਾਹੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)ddahu hovai dhosatee bha(n)ddahu chalai raahu ||
lines.translation: Woman becomes his friend; through woman, the future generations come.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡੁ ਮੁਆ ਭੰਡੁ ਭਾਲੀਐ ਭੰਡਿ ਹੋਵੈ ਬੰਧਾਨੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)dd muaa bha(n)dd bhaaleeaai bha(n)dd hovai ba(n)dhaan ||
lines.translation: When his woman dies, he seeks another woman; to woman he is bound.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਕਿਉ ਮੰਦਾ ਆਖੀਐ ਜਿਤੁ ਜੰਮਹਿ ਰਾਜਾਨ ॥
lines.transliteration: so kiau ma(n)dhaa aakheeaai jit ja(n)meh raajaan ||
lines.translation: So why call her bad? From her, kings are born.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭੰਡਹੁ ਹੀ ਭੰਡੁ ਊਪਜੈ ਭੰਡੈ ਬਾਝੁ ਨ ਕੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bha(n)ddahu hee bha(n)dd uoopajai bha(n)ddai baajh na koi ||
lines.translation: From woman, woman is born; without woman, there would be no one at all.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਭੰਡੈ ਬਾਹਰਾ ਏਕੋ ਸਚਾ ਸੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak bha(n)ddai baaharaa eko sachaa soi ||
lines.translation: O Nanak, only the True Lord is without a woman.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਦਾ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ਭਾਗਾ ਰਤੀ ਚਾਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: jit mukh sadhaa saalaaheeaai bhaagaa ratee chaar ||
lines.translation: That mouth which praises the Lord continually is blessed and beautiful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇ ਮੁਖ ਊਜਲੇ ਤਿਤੁ ਸਚੈ ਦਰਬਾਰਿ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak te mukh uoojale tit sachai dharabaar ||2||
lines.translation: O Nanak, those faces shall be radiant in the Court of the True Lord. ||2||

structure: First, it begins by naming how thoroughly human life is bound up with woman.
Then, it confronts contempt directly and calls it irrational in the face of reality.
Finally, it ends by lifting the mouth that praises the Lord rather than degrading His creation.
